annotation_description: Discarded Enduring Curiosity (a very powerful card with flash, card draw engine, and death resilience) over Flitterwing Nuisance, which is a 1/1 flyer that requires additional mana investment to draw cards. While having a duplicate Curiosity makes this somewhat defensible, Enduring Curiosity is significantly more impactful than Flitterwing Nuisance, and keeping both copies gives more chances to deploy this game-winning threat.

Casting Slickshot Show-Off in the precombat main phase is suboptimal when holding multiple combat tricks (Dreadmaw's Ire, Full Bore, Might of the Meek, Bulk Up). The opponent has only 1 Island untapped (no counterspell mana), so there's minimal risk of it being countered. However, playing it pre-combat reveals information unnecessarily and means the opponent knows about it before declaring blockers. More importantly, Slickshot Show-Off has Plot for {1}{R} - plotting it would let you deploy it for free on a later turn while keeping mana open for combat tricks. With only 2 Mountains available, casting Show-Off uses all mana and prevents casting any combat tricks this turn. Plotting it would also use all mana but set up a much more explosive future turn where you can cast Show-Off for free and chain multiple pump spells.

Discarded a basic Island while severely mana-screwed with only 1 land on the battlefield. With 3 lands in an 8-card hand and desperate need for mana development, every land is critical. Enduring Curiosity (4 mana, already one in graveyard) is the obvious discard as it's uncastable for many turns.

Casting Bulk Up (a combat trick that doubles power) during precombat main phase is wasteful in multiple ways. First, it tips off the opponent before blocks are declared. Second and more critically, with Leyline of Resonance in hand (which copies instants/sorceries targeting a single creature you control), GLM47 should have played Leyline of Resonance first to get double value from combat tricks. Additionally, casting combat tricks before combat means the opponent sees the pump and can plan accordingly. With only 1 Island on the opponent's board, there's minimal counterplay risk, but the sequencing is still wrong. The Leyline of Resonance would double every subsequent combat trick (Bulk Up, Full Bore, Dreadmaw's Ire, Might of the Meek), providing enormous value over the game.

GLM47 attacked with only Stadium Headliner instead of all creatures. The opponent has only 1 untapped Island and no creatures to block. Slickshot Show-Off has flying and haste, and with pump spells in hand (Dreadmaw's Ire, Full Bore, Might of the Meek), attacking with both creatures would deal significantly more damage. With Slickshot Show-Off attacking unblocked (flying, no flyers on opponent's side), casting pump spells on it would trigger its +2/+0 ability per noncreature spell. For example, attacking all and then casting Dreadmaw's Ire on Slickshot would make it 1+2+2=5 power with trample, plus the Headliner's 1 damage and Mobilize token's 1 damage = 7+ damage. Even without pumps, sending both would deal at least 3 damage (1+1 from Headliner+token, 1 from Slickshot) instead of 2. Holding back Slickshot for no reason when the opponent has no blockers and minimal interaction (1 untapped Island could represent Essence Scatter but Show-Off is already on board) wastes significant damage.

Discarding Essence Scatter over Soulstone Sanctuary when severely behind on mana development. Soulstone Sanctuary only provides colorless mana, while the hand is full of colored-mana-intensive spells (Kaito at 2UB, Enduring Curiosity at 2UU, Deep-Cavern Bat at 1B). Essence Scatter at 1U could be crucial for stopping opponent's threats while catching up on board.

Casting Stadium Headliner (a creature) before combat is suboptimal when holding multiple combat tricks (Dreadmaw's Ire, Full Bore, Might of the Meek, Turn Inside Out). The player already has Stadium Headliner and Slickshot Show-Off on board to attack with. Casting a creature pre-combat gives the opponent information and doesn't benefit from haste. More importantly, Slickshot Show-Off gets +2/+0 for each noncreature spell cast, so the player should attack first, then cast pump spells during combat for maximum damage. Casting the creature pre-combat doesn't trigger Slickshot's ability and uses mana that could be held for combat tricks. The second Stadium Headliner won't have haste and can't attack this turn anyway, so it should be cast post-combat to preserve mana flexibility during combat.

Left one Stadium Headliner back when the opponent had no creatures to block and only 1 untapped Island. Attacking with all 3 creatures would have generated an additional Mobilize token and dealt more damage (5 instead of ~3-4) with zero risk.

Dreadmaw's Ire gives +2/+2 and trample to an attacking creature, but the trample is largely irrelevant on a flying Slickshot Show-Off, and the artifact destruction trigger is useless against an opponent with no artifacts. Full Bore would have given +3/+2 (1 more damage), and Might of the Meek would have drawn a card while still triggering prowess, which is more valuable than 2 extra damage when opponent is at 15 life.

Cast Turn Inside Out targeting Slickshot Show-Off during precombat main instead of during combat. While lethal is available either way (Slickshot + 2 Headliners + 2 tokens = enough damage), casting pump spells before combat gives the opponent more information and a window to respond before attackers are declared. With only 1 untapped Island the risk is small, but it's still strictly worse sequencing.

Redirect Lightning was cast unnecessarily on the stack targeting their own Turn Inside Out, wasting a card (and likely 5 life or 2 mana). GLM47 already had lethal damage available: Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying haste) + Turn Inside Out (+3/+0, triggers +2/+0) = 6 power, plus Full Bore (+3/+2, triggers +2/+0) = 11 power flying, which is lethal against 8 life. The extra spell was completely unnecessary.

Redirected Turn Inside Out (+3/+0) to Stadium Headliner instead of Slickshot Show-Off. Slickshot Show-Off has flying (harder to block) and already benefits from noncreature spell triggers (+2/+0 each). With the opponent at 8 life, maximizing damage on the evasive flyer would be more effective for pushing lethal damage.

Missed lethal by not playing Fire Nation Palace before combat. Fire Nation Palace enters untapped (controls basic Mountains), providing {R} to cast Full Bore on Slickshot Show-Off during combat. Slickshot would get +2/+0 from noncreature trigger and +3/+2 from Full Bore, becoming 6/4 flying. Combined with 2 Stadium Headliners (2 damage) and 2 Mobilize tokens (2 damage), that's 10 total damage against opponent's 8 life — lethal.
